abstract: Physical stressors profoundly influence cellular behavior by triggering coordinated stress-response programs that regulate signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate. Here, we present CellStressDB (https://cellstressdb.omic.tech), an AI-powered database for exploring cellular responses to physical stressors. The current release contains data from 131 transcriptomic studies, with 2 364 816 cell and 1205 bulk sample observations from human and mouse across nine physical-stress classes and 21 tissue categories. Data and analyses are organized into 2848 indexed analysis entries across 71 canonical species-tissue-stress contexts with detailed exposure conditions retained. CellStressDB provides ontology-guided cell-type annotation through 22 tissue-aware classifiers and incorporates 941 Geneformer checkpoints for context-specific in silico perturbation. Analyses include stress-response programs, differential gene expression, functional enrichment, regulon activity, cell-type composition, and cell-cell communication where applicable, with candidate compound prioritization, downloadable datasets and models, and analysis of user-provided transcriptomic data. Annotation evaluation and known-factor recovery analyses indicated context-dependent performance and coverage across biological settings. The mouse radiation-intestine example identifies Stat1 as a candidate regulator of radiation-induced intestinal injury supported by independent experimental evidence. Overall, CellStressDB provides an integrated, AI-enabled framework for exploring and interpreting cellular responses to physical stressors and generating testable hypotheses.
